title: Rollout Insights & Cohort Diffing for Console Rollouts
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver a first-class Rollout Observability surface in the Redwood Console that gives engineers and PMs clear, defensible signals during canary rollouts, A/B experiments, and shadow traffic runs, and integrates with auto-rollback policies. The experience must surface per-route metrics, cohort diff views (statistical and visual), request traces for regression investigation, and quality signals tied to eval prompt sets.

Scope: 1) Per-route dashboard tiles (P50/P95/P99 latency, request rate, error rate, token consumption); 2) Cohort comparison view with selectable metrics and statistical test results (support for sequential testing and Bayesian confidence intervals); 3) Trace drilldowns linked to example payloads and model variant mapping; 4) Shadow traffic explorer with sampling controls and traffic split visualization; 5) Auto-rollback telemetry and audit trail (reason, triggered thresholds, manual override).

Key user problems addressed: unclear signal during short canaries, difficulty attributing errors to model vs prompt changes, slow investigation path from metrics -> trace -> diff, and lack of transparent rollback rationale for SREs and product owners.

Non-goals for MVP: full cohort-level model output diffing (NLG semantic diffs beyond token-level metrics), long-term aggregated longitudinal experiments (>90 days retention) — these will be scoped to follow-ups.

Data & instrumentation notes: We'll instrument the serving runtime to emit per-request metadata (route, model_version, cohort_id, latency_ms, token_count, error_code, trace_id). To keep cardinality under control, cohort_id will be limited to canonical rollout IDs and experiment IDs. Sampling for traces will be 1% by default with an on-demand capture for flagged cohorts. Metrics buckets and histogram config will align with existing Console telemetry conventions.

Trade-offs discussed: 1) Full-text diffs provide high-fidelity quality signals but add storage and privacy concerns — deferred to post-MVP. 2) Statistical approach: team recommended Bayesian sequential testing for earlier decisions with explicit credible intervals; engineering raised compute/complexity concerns so MVP will include both a simple t-test/MW test and a toggle to enable Bayesian analysis for prioritized experiments.

Success metrics: adoption by 3 pilot customers within first 8 weeks, average time-to-detect regression during canary reduced from 47m -> <15m in internal playbook runs, and >80% of auto-rollback activations contain a linked trace and audit entry.
